clue.text: Sweep? Grand prize: young dog, domesticated

explanation.surface: A lottery sweep with a puppy as its grand prize.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweep is the grey dog glove puppet from the long-running British children's TV show Sooty, so the young dog in the wordplay is a sly echo of the definition; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweep is one particular glove puppet, so the answer names the class he belongs to.

clue.text: Lose it when a grandmother’s stuck under overturned Portaloo?

explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal idioms for losing self-control, whether in anger or excitement.

clue.text: Needing to tour base, punctual or late?

explanation.definitionFit: Late can mean former, and a one-time champion is a former one.

clue.text: Superior dentures should not have a rattle

explanation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: shaking someone's composure, the figurative sense of rattle, not the noise false teeth make.

clue.text: Tripe I scribbled about Oscar award-winning actor

clue.text: Tense, strain and wheeze

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wheeze' reads as a breathing noise, but it is the British noun for a clever scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A British colloquial sense: wheeze means a clever scheme or dodge, not the chesty sound.

clue.text: Ready for Vladimir‘s problem with the French?

blocks.note: 'there's the rub': a rub is a problem

explanation.definitionFit: Slang plus a typical name: 'the ready' means cash, and Vladimir stands for any Russian, whose cash is in Russia's currency.

clue.text: Insects swirling misled radar

indicators.note: swirling letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the answer names a common butterfly species, and the clue gives only the broad category.

clue.text: Nuisance is returning for start of the film, making one gloomy

kept as it is, before turning round
first letter of 'the', which is swapped out of PEST

explanation.walkthrough: The T that begins 'the' is the letter replaced, not the start of the film: PEST becomes PES + SI.
explanation.definitionFit: A pessimist is one gloomy about how things will turn out.

clue.text: Money and hollow moneymen essentially controlling every area of music publishing

blocks.note: tin is old British slang for money
a pan is a hollow in the ground, as in a salt pan
every = all

the two central letters of MONEYMEN

clue.text: Composite ultimately added to cavity in part of tooth

blocks.note: a dent is a hollow or cavity
kept as it is
last letter of 'composite'

explanation.definitionFit: Dentine is the hard tissue under the enamel, forming most of a tooth.

clue.text: Brainstorming meeting, light and mostly helpful

kind = helpful

explanation.surface: A description of a brainstorming session that was light and fairly useful.

clue.text: Poet uncovered sonnet written by daughter

clue.text: Among other things, Alicia disheartened with Milan team

clue.text: Inside house, husband and son binding English reference book

clue.text: Famous, on edge and cautious, covering head

clue.text: Lying at home, as revenue depleted

as = since, 'as it's raining'
REVENUE emptied of its middle leaves its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone lying about at home while their income runs out.

clue.text: US right-wingers, once called “old cheats”

clue.text: Make fun of odd bits of glam music subgenre

first and third letters of GLAM

clue.text: Setter unhappy about coming round for evening cocktail?

clue.text: Race ending in victory, visibly emotional

clue.text: Cabinet politician checking that man’s medical records?
